title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-36
content:
Quick notes / scratchpad - GPU ops (Priya)

Date: 2026-02-28 (last touch 2026-03-01)
Context: personal running list for infra tasks around GPU capacity, networking oddities, and follow-ups for Dedicated customers. Mostly reminders + commands I used.

Top of day
- Morning health: check node groups + GPU telemetry: nvidia-smi on problematic hosts (see host-list below).
- Check autoscaler metrics (queue length + pod pending time) for gpu-pool-prod. Noticed spike 02/27 22:10 UTC — correlate with AcmePay batch jobs.

Immediate TODOs (priority order)
1) Rotate driver on gpu-nodepool-3 (NVIDIA 535 -> 537) - schedule maintenance window with CS (AcmePay). Impact: rolling reboot of 6 nodes, plan to drain one at a time. Ticket: JIRA-ENGOPS-842.
   - Commands: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data; ssh to node -> sudo apt update && sudo apt install nvidia-driver-537; reboot; verify nvidia-smi.
2) Investigate OOMs for large-quantized models on dedicated-1: start with pod logs + dmesg for OOM-killer. Linked PR: github:pr/5123 (alloc bump workaround).
3) Tune cluster-autoscaler scale-down delay (current 10m) -> reduce to 5m for spot-backed nodes to free capacity quicker during bursts. Prototype in staging, measure thrash.
4) Network: flaky connections observed between us-west-2 compute and storage (nfs-gateway-02). Packet drops ~0.5% during peak. Opened infra-net ticket with cloud provider (case# 35821).

Host list to check (yesterday failures)
- gpu-prod-07 (us-west-2) - repeated CUDA driver resets, kernel logs show GPU reset: GPU 0.
- gpu-prod-11 (us-west-2) - high ECC errors on MIG partitions.
- gpu-dedicated-02 (eu-west-1) - OOM killer observed once at 03:12 UTC.

Commands / quick checklist I ran
- kubectl get pods -n inference -o wide --field-selector=status.phase=Pending
- kubectl describe pod <pod> | grep -A5 Events
- ssh ops@gpu-prod-07 'sudo journalctl -u nvidia-persistenced -n 200'
- sudo dmesg | egrep -i 'oom|killed process|gpu reset'
- nvidia-smi -q -d ECC

Notes / Observations
- gpu-pool-prod baseline utilization: 72% avg last 48h, but 90% during 22:00-00:00 UTC. SLO risk window for low-latency customers (hosted-api).
- Some jobs are not requesting GPU resources correctly -> falling back to CPU, causing queuing pressure. Need to audit Helm charts for model-serving job templates.
- Model-ops ran a new quantized Llama variant yesterday; initial tests show 5% higher peak memory than expected. Add to regression checklist.

Follow-ups & People to ping
- @Samir: confirm maintenance blackout windows for Dedicated customers (AcmePay + FinLedger) before driver rotation. (samir@redwood.ai)
- @Jorge: can you run a night-run stress test on staging with spot eviction turned on? Results by Friday.
- @Model-Ops: add the quantized model to the eval set and run memory profiler.

Meeting notes (standup 2026-02-28)
- Reported increased latency for small-chat endpoint; root cause likely queueing at GPU pool. Action: temporary scale up of gpu-pool-prod by +2 nodes (spot) til driver rotation complete.
- Agreed to add more descriptive alerts for pending pods > 2m in inference namespace.

Open questions / unresolved
- Why did MIG partitions show ECC increase on gpu-prod-11? HW issue or software regression after kernel upgrade 537? Need vendor support to run full diagnostics.
- Can we safely decrease scale-down delay without causing excessive node churn for short jobs? Need A/B test.

Docs to update
- /confluence/Infra/GPU-Ops: add driver rotation runbook (include cordon/drain steps + roll-back).
- Internal KB: how to interpret ECC reports from nvidia-smi (add screenshots).

Personal TODO (follow-up times)
- Today 10:00: call with Samir to align schedule (15m).
- Today 13:00: run driver rotation on staging cluster (gpu-staging-02).
- Today 16:30: review results from Jorge's stress test (if available).

Quick snippets to copy into tickets
- "Observed repeated GPU resets on gpu-prod-07 between 02/27 21:50-22:20 UTC. Kernel logs show: 'GPU reset: Xid 31'. Requesting vendor diagnostics and driver patch test."
- "Pending pods in inference namespace >3m for N=12 in last 24h — consider increasing burst capacity or tuning batching config."

Done / Completed items (recent)
- Pushed hotfix to autoscaler config to prefer on-demand for critical customers (deployed 2026-02-26).
- Completed small change in K8s pod spec to set requests.gpu for model-run jobs (reliable tests pass).

End of scratchpad.

Random notes to self: coffee, backup laptop before big node reboots, take screenshots of monitoring graphs before making changes.
